texts.5a0591c63a6d: Health iQ wishes to apply for access to monthly HES IP, OP and A&E data to support its health intelligence platform ‘Vantage’. Health iQ has been recieving data from the HSCIC for a number of years and this request is for the continuation of data Health iQ currently receive. Vantage is an online tool, which allows users to analyse healthcare data, derive a range of insights and produce reports to support the improvement of clinical outcomes and optimisation of operational efficiency within a healthcare setting. It incorporates aggregate HES, QOF and primary care prescribing data, all viewable at a GP Practice level. The tools target audience is NHS organisations, and is available directly to them however the NHS is increasingly looking to industry to support it in the provision of evidence for service improvement, and hence Health-IQ also offer the tool to a limited number of pharmaceutical companies based on their agreeing to license terms and conditions, which include submitting to training in information governance and the restriction of the use of the tool to the uses outlined in this document. These companies will in turn provide free access to the tool to their NHS customers as part of what is known as a ‘value beyond the pill’ service, ie offering more to the benefit of the NHS than simply medication. The tool is also available directly to the NHS (CCGS, CSUs and Trusts), and is currently used by a number of such organisations. As Vantage is a tool, licensed to a number of customers who us it in a range of ways, Health-IQ will outline the purpose of processing data by first outlining the main uses of the tool in a general sense, secondly providing case studies of how the tool has specifically been used over the past 12 months, and finally provide some specific uses that will be carried out over the next 12 months. 1. Overall purpose: Vantage provides NHS commissioners and providers with reliable robust information on the delivery of healthcare services within their local health economies and national/local comparative information including benchmarking data. : • Commissioning intelligence and benchmarking • Programme budgeting and healthcare utilization analysis • Impact of risk stratification approaches • Healthcare modelling of pathway and system redesign initiatives • Provider efficiency and productivity analysis • Healthcare demand and referral analysis • Heath care needs assessment information • Public health and disease prevalence information by locality • Predictive modelling and trend analysis • Evaluations of new healthcare interventions 2. Specific case studies for the past 12 months: Case study 1: West Midlands SCN PD network July 2014 Vantage tool has been used by the West Midlands strategic clinical network (SCN) to complete a comprehensive baseline on the current management of Parkinson disease. The following data was collated as part of overall report produced by the SCN for its meeting in July 2014: • Quantifying Parkinson disease burden by calculating total admissions, bed days and tariff cost for a specific set of ICD-10 codes, split by region/CCG. • Benchmarking CCG and/or hospital costs for Parkinson’s disease related activity measured against standard hospitalization indicators such as readmission rate, length-of-stay, pre and post-op bed days, excess bed days, first-to-follow-up ratio, emergency admissions • Mapping the cost to CCG of all PD referrals vs estimated CCG PD disease prevalence. The report has led to development of West Midlands PD action plan and has already led to development new disease pathway and standardization of PD commissioning approach across the West Midlands CCGs which will over time reduce health inequalities. Case study 2: Quality Standards in relation to Surgical site infection rates NICE guidelines on the management on surgical site infection rates QS49 - Issued: October 2013 http://publications.nice.org.uk/surgical-site-infection-qs49 requires all NHS providers conducting surgical procedures to monitor surgical site infection rates. Providers are also expected to utilise surgical site infection data to provide feedback to relevant staff and stakeholders for continuous improvement through adjustment of clinical practice The Vantage tool has been used by a number of NHS trusts to benchmark surgical site infection rates (Including post-discharge infections) and to facilitate internal quality improvement discussions. Vantage has supported NHS trusts with a higher than average rate identify key clinical areas to focus quality improvement activity leading to a commensurate reduction in surgical site infection rates. Case study 3: Pharmaceutical company working in partnership with NHS to improve the management of Diabetes A major pharmaceutical company provides Vantage tool to its NHS commissioners as part of value added offering in Diabetes. The data provided enables local CCGs to benchmark performance in a range of parameters and has also enabled them to focus resources on those care processes which would have the biggest impact on the overall outcomes achieved by local patients. The pharmaceutical company has also developed a diabetes audit tool and patient education resources. The pharmaceutical company utilises Vantage data to identify which CCGs may have a potential need for its non-promotional service offerings. 3. Specific uses of the tool over the coming 12 months Example 1: Supporting CCGs across the West Midlands in building business cases for the implementation of new community-based epilepsy service. Vantage will enable them to quantify their own local spend on eplipsy referrals, as well as additional unscheduled spend through emergency admissions. The system would then be used to conduct a post-implementation review (at least 6 months) of the same outcomes, to quantify the impact of the new service. The service will be provided for free to the CCGs by one of our pharmaceutical customers. Example 2: Vantage will be used to provide evidence for the need for inpatient hospital guidelines for the treatment of moderate/severe parkinsons patients. The tool will be used to analyse non-elective admissions and readmission trends and associated costs. This will be provided as a free service to hospitals by one of our pharmaceutical customers. Example 3: Vantage will be used to prepare a set of diabetes service reports for every CCG across the UK. These reports will outline diabetes activity, QOF achievement and GP prescribing, and will be broken down by GP practice. This will support the improvement of diabetes service provision at a GP level, and is provided as a free service to CCGs by a pharmaceutical customer.
